title: Open Tender for Douglas Valley Outdoor Recreation and Adventure Tourism Market Research, Branding, Website Development & Wayfinding
description: South Lanarkshire Council seeks a Creative Consultancy to deliver a Market Assessment, Branding Strategy, Website Development, Content Library and Wayfinding Strategy for the Douglas Valley Outdoor Recreation and Adventure Tourism initiative within the Hagshaw Energy Cluster. 1. Market Assessment Review existing project documentation and identify implications for branding, marketing and website development. Analyse visitor data, market trends and audience segmentation, including visitor case studies. Benchmark comparable projects and destinations. Provide recommendations to inform branding, website design, content and future marketing activity. 2. Branding Development Develop and consult on three branding concepts before producing a final identity. Create brand assets including logo, name, tagline, colours, fonts and digital/print applications. Produce brand guidelines covering signage, interpretation, promotional materials and integration with existing site branding. Include recommendations for social media and future marketing activity. 3. Website Design, Build and Launch Create a branded website promoting Douglas Valley as a destination to live, work, visit and enjoy, supporting ambitions to attract up to 100,000 annual visits by 2036. Develop a scalable, content-led website with a planned lifespan of ten years. Include six core pages: Home, About, Explore, See & Stay, News and Contact. The Explore section will feature an interactive map highlighting key recreational and active travel routes, points of interest and route information including distance, elevation, difficulty and duration. Build the site on an accessible CMS suitable for community and council users. Host on a secure UK-based platform with maintenance and support arrangements. Ensure accessibility compliance and provide flexible management of route information and temporary diversions. 4. Photography and Video Library Establish a copyright-cleared library of photography and short-form video content for web, social media and print use. Source content through community engagement, youth-focused workshops and professional photography where required. Content will reflect identified visitor segments and feature strong people-focused imagery. Coverage will include renewable energy, local communities, nature, heritage and identity, local economy and outdoor recreation. Key locations include Coalbur

title: CeTPD Laboratory Information Management System
description: The Centre for Targeted Protein Degradation (CeTPD) is an academic research center focused on translational chemical biology, currently housing ~60 researchers and technicians across disciplines and experience levels (undergraduate, post graduate students, post-docs, (senior) staff scientists, Principal Investigators). The requirement is a software solution, for all research staff, that provides Laboratory Information Management System (LIMs) capability. This broadly includes scientist electronic lab notebook (across disciplines), reagent inventory and management, compound inventory and management and ideally some capability for processed data databasing and rudimentary visualisation. We are seeking to procure a secure, cloud-based design and Laboratory Information Management System to support collaborative drug discovery workflows. The solution is expected to deliver; - An integrated platform for electronic lab notebooks, reagent inventory management, compound registration and management and ideally data visualisation. - The system must accommodate the needs of scientists in both chemical and biological sciences and their respective workflows. - The system must accommodate that Users may require access relevant to both chemical biological sciences workflows within the same user area. - Seamless integration with existing computational workflows - Seamless integration with third-party applications and/or databases - A secure, stable and scalable cloud deployment which Complies with the University and collaborator cybersecurity, information governance and GDPR requirements Meets with strict performance, reliability and governance standards Meets with the functional and non-functional requirements of the CeTPD (as outlined below) - Improved operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and scalability to support future growth and evolving scientific needs

title: General Office Supplies 2027
description: This Framework Agreement is for the provision of General Office Supplies, including Stationery, Office Paper, Electronic Office Supplies (EOS), Catering Goods and Consumables, Janitorial and Hygiene products to the Scottish public sector. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Scottish Ministers (including Agencies), Scottish Non-Departmental Public Bodies, offices in the Scottish Administration which are not ministerial offices, cross-border public authorities within the meaning of section 88(5) of the Scotland Act 1998, The Office for the Secretary of State for Scotland, the Scottish Parliamentary Corporate Body, councils constituted under section 2 of the Local Government etc. (Scotland) Act 1994, bodies registered as social landlords under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2001, Scottish health boards or special health boards, Student Loans Company Limited, the Commissioner of Northern Lighthouse operating as the Northern Lighthouse Board, Scottish Futures Trust, Equality and Human Rights Commission, Business Stream Ltd, the Business Gateway National Unit at the Convention of Scottish Local Authorities, further or higher education institutions being fundable bodies within the meaning of section 6 of the further and Higher Education (Scotland) Act 2005, any public body established by or under the Scotland Act 1998 or any Act of the Scottish Parliament, any association of or formed by one or more of the foregoing, bodies financed wholly or mainly by one or more of the foregoing, bodies subject to management supervision by one or more of the foregoing and bodies more than half of the board of directors or members of which, or, in the case of a group of individuals, more than half of those individuals, being appointed by one or more of the foregoing. In addition to the contracting authorities listed, the framework agreement will be available to charities entered on the Scottish Charity Register and voluntary organisations entered on the Membership Database of the Scottish Council for Voluntary Organisations. title: Glasgow Business Growth Framework - Phase 4
description: Glasgow City Council (the Council) requires a framework of suppliers to deliver a range of business growth consultancy services to eligible organisations across the city to aide a sustainable growth agenda and improve business start-up and survival rates. title: The Provision of a Mental Health Crisis Text Support Service on behalf of NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board
buyer: NHS CHESHIRE AND MERSEYSIDE INTEGRATED CARE BOARD
description: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside is seeking to engage with the market regarding the provision of an all-age, 24-hour, 7 days a week/ 365 days a year Mental Health Crisis Text Service across Cheshire and Merseyside. The service will provide immediate, accessible and inclusive text-based support for individuals experiencing a mental health crisis and will operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The service is intended to be fully integrated with NHS 111 (Mental Health Option) and local crisis response pathways, ensuring seamless access to urgent mental health support and onward referral where required. The service has been developed in line with NHS England guidance on urgent and emergency mental health care and supports the objectives of the NHS Long Term Plan, the Urgent and Emergency Care Recovery Plan, and national suicide prevention priorities. It aims to improve access to crisis support for people who may experience barriers to traditional services, including those affected by stigma, communication difficulties, disability, sensory needs, or geographical isolation across the region's diverse urban and rural communities. The term of the contract is 2 years, with the option to extend for 2 further periods of up to one year each. The extension options are not guaranteed and will be subject to ongoing service requirements, satisfactory performance, available funding and approval by the Authority. The maximum total contract value, including both potential extensions, is £1,400,000 ex VAT.
